about: Does the studio catch a film's motion glitches itself? Five 60-second character films, each asking for the things that broke three Duchess episodes on 2026-10-07: a character going into and out of something, behind something, turning round, a hand that gives or takes, a narrated look, a change of light. Arms: 'base' and 'base2' are the studio before (the same checkout twice, for the noise between two runs of one prompt), 'review' is the film-review worktree (the whole film a frame a second and the strip tool for the author, what the drawing code shows, the reader after the author's last turn and its one fix turn). Compare glitches per film (studio/defects.py over each arm's films, and by eye), Claude's time and the film's whole time.

prompts.prompt: A 60-second cartoon for kids. A small ginger kitten named Biscuit does not want the family to go on holiday without him. While a pair of hands packs a suitcase, Biscuit climbs into it and hides under a jumper, with only his tail showing. The hands lift the jumper, find him, and put him on the floor. He walks round the suitcase, hops back in from the other side, and this time pulls the lid shut over himself. A deadpan narrator describes all of it as if it were a serious expedition. End on the hands packing a tiny kitten-sized suitcase.

A 60-second cartoon for kids. It starts to rain. A big shaggy dog called Captain runs to his dog house, which is clearly too small for him, and tries three ways of getting in: head first, backwards, and finally sideways. A snail watches from the roof. In the end Captain sits outside in the rain, and holds the dog house over his head like a hat. The narrator is calm and precise, like a sports commentator. Show the afternoon turning to evening by the end.

A 60-second cartoon for kids. A rabbit magician in a small cape does a show for an audience of three hens. He steps behind a curtain and comes out the other side wearing a top hat. He turns round to bow to each hen in turn. He climbs into a box, and a hand saws the box in half, the two halves roll apart, and the rabbit pops out of the top hat on the table instead. The hens are not impressed until the very end. A narrator introduces each trick in one short sentence before it happens.

A 60-second cartoon for kids. A little bear called Moss will not go to bed. A grown-up's hand turns off the lamp, and Moss turns it back on. The hand tucks him in, and he slides out of the other side of the bed and hides behind the curtain, in the toy chest, and under the bed, and is found each time. The narrator says what Moss is thinking: he looks at the moon in the window, and decides the moon is not asleep either. He falls asleep in the toy chest and the hand carries him to bed.

A 60-second cartoon for kids. A parcel arrives: a hand puts a big cardboard box on the kitchen floor and leaves. A hamster called Dot looks at the box from her wheel, then gets down, walks all the way round it, goes in through a hole in its side and comes out of the top. She pushes things out of the box one by one: a sock, a spoon, a rubber duck. At the end she has moved in, and the box has a little door, a window with a curtain, and a doormat. The narrator reads it like the news.
